scope_declines.name: §3, Example 3.17: the sl2 duality computation
scope_declines.reason: Not needed: the pair's sl2 examples use the explicit Verma action and projective structure, not the sl2 contragredient-duality table.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 4.8 and 4.12: P_λ ↠ M_λ ↠ L_λ and the comparison of the representing object with P_λ
scope_declines.reason: These homework problems refine the construction of projective covers; the pair only needs existence, uniqueness and the Hom-counting property, all proved from Theorem 4.4 and Corollary 4.9.

scope_declines.name: §3, Lemma 3.14 and Lemma 3.16 in the sl2 block
scope_declines.reason: The B page derives the sl2 orthogonality table from the displayed flag multiplicities and BGG reciprocity; the general duality lemmas are not consumed there.

scope_declines.name: §3, Construction 3.17 and Exercise 3.18: translation out of the most singular block and Ξ_μ ≅ P_μ
scope_declines.reason: The most singular block and the identification of Ξ_μ with the big projective are not used by any claim or example of this pair.

scope_declines.name: §§5–7 (spherical maximal function, maximal functions, exercises), pp. 13–22
scope_declines.reason: These sections concern maximal operators supplied by the published FR-9/FR-12/FR-13 material; no FR-14 item states or consumes them.

scope_declines.name: §1, Lemma 1.8: a short exact sequence with standardly filtered quotient
scope_declines.reason: The pair does not use this criterion for extensions; the corresponding statements are proved directly from the multiplicity formula and the exact sequences of the items that need them.

scope_declines.name: Sections 5-6, Folner's theorem, Peter-Weyl, and separation of points by characters
scope_declines.reason: Point separation and compact-group orthogonality are developed inversion-first on the duality pair and must not be imported into this foundation, whose design removes the circular compact-group route.

scope_declines.name: §20.1–20.2, restricted duality and costandard modules of the sl2 block
scope_declines.reason: The sl2 examples compute directly with Verma flags and projective covers; the duality table is not needed at this size.

scope_declines.name: §§10-14: Bochner, inversion, Plancherel, inversion-based duality, structure and exactness
scope_declines.reason: The design keeps Bochner, inversion and Plancherel on the FR-16 pair and biduality and exactness on FR-17; none of this may enter the inversion-free FR-15 foundation.

scope_declines.name: 34B: every character arises from a regular maximal ideal of L1(G), identifying the dual with the maximal-ideal space
scope_declines.reason: The L1/Gelfand identification of the character space is FR-16 material; this foundation defines the dual directly as continuous homomorphisms and deliberately avoids the group-algebra route.

scope_declines.name: §3, Theorem 3.13: translation between blocks with the same facet is an equivalence
scope_declines.reason: The pair only needs the wall behaviour of standards and the adjunction; the equivalence of blocks of the same facet is not among its claims or examples.

scope_declines.name: §20.1, Lemma 20.1 and Corollary 20.2: vanishing of Ext^i for objects free over U(n−), and for standardly filtered objects
scope_declines.reason: The pair only needs Ext^1(Δ(μ), ∇(ν)) = 0 and its long-exact-sequence consequence for standardly filtered X, which are proved from Lin Chen's Lemmas 3.14 and 3.16; the general Ext^i vanishing has no consumer in this pair.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Theorem C.11: characters of a compact abelian group separate points and form an orthonormal basis of L2
scope_declines.reason: Compact-group character completeness is obtained there from inversion and Plancherel; importing it here would reintroduce the circular compact-group route the design removes.

scope_declines.name: Dyadic decomposition proof of Theorem 7.1 for q > q_0, (80)–(84), printed pp. 45–47
scope_declines.reason: The scaffold follows the Williams §11.3 fractional-integration route, which is valid at the endpoint q_0; the dyadic pieces (84) do not decay at q = q_0, so the dyadic argument is retained only as an independent treatment and cross-check, and no item is built from it.

scope_declines.name: §20.2, Theorem 20.3: standard filteredness is equivalent to Ext^1(X, M^∨_μ) = 0 for all μ
scope_declines.reason: Only the forward direction is used, and it is proved directly by induction on the flag length in lem-hom-to-costandards-counts-verma-flag-factors; the converse characterization has no consumer in this pair.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Lemma C.15: Riemann-Lebesgue for measures absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure
scope_declines.reason: The LCA Riemann-Lebesgue lemma is a consequence of joint evaluation proved on the planned Bochner/inversion pair, not an FR-15 claim.

scope_declines.name: Section 7.2, Example 7.7 and Exercises 7.8-7.10: duals of Z(p-infinity), Jp and Qp
scope_declines.reason: p-adic and Prufer-group duals are outside the commissioned FR-15 scope, and no scaffolded item, B-page example or registered consumer of this pair uses them.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Theorem C.12 and C.13: biduality and annihilator exactness
scope_declines.reason: These are the planned duality pair's own results; the examples on this page use only the concrete dual computations listed above.

scope_declines.name: Further remarks: Theorem 7.4 (L^2 bound from α-dimensionality) and Lemma 7.5 (Schur's test), printed pp. 47–49
scope_declines.reason: Not consumed: the page's slice L^2 bound is Plancherel with an explicit bounded multiplier and the kernel decay is stationary phase, so neither Schur's test nor the abstract L^2 bound is needed by any item.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Theorem C.13: the remaining annihilator exactness identities (G-hat/H-perp, H1-perp + H2-perp, H-perp-perp)
scope_declines.reason: These identities are proved there from biduality and belong to the exactness development of the planned duality pair.

scope_declines.name: Finite abelian groups: characters, orthogonality, Peter–Weyl and Fourier inversion, pp. 1–8
scope_declines.reason: This is finite-abelian Fourier theory of the FR-15/FR-16 type; no FR-14 item states or uses it, and the page's FR-14 inventory is complete without it.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Theorem C.10 and Theorem C.12: inversion and Pontryagin biduality
scope_declines.reason: Inversion and biduality are the subjects of the planned Bochner/inversion and duality pairs; the FR-15 foundation is deliberately inversion-free.

scope_declines.name: Section 7.3, Exercise 7.11: characters of subgroups of Rn extend to Rn
scope_declines.reason: Character extension from closed subgroups is proved there from biduality and annihilator exactness; the FR-15 foundation is deliberately biduality-free and needs no extension theorem.

scope_declines.name: 34E: remark on the sign convention relating the character a_M to the Fourier transform
scope_declines.reason: A convention remark about the transform normalisation; the library fixes its LCA transform convention on the FR-6 and FR-16 pages, and no FR-15 claim depends on this remark.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Example C.14(3)-(4): duals of locally compact fields and of Qp
scope_declines.reason: Local-field and p-adic duals are not commissioned for this pair, and neither the A page nor the four B examples consume them.

scope_declines.name: Section 1.2, Proposition 1.23 and Theorem 1.28: the closed subgroups of R and the structure of Rn/H
scope_declines.reason: The closed-subgroup classification of R and Rn is not consumed by any FR-15 claim: this pair needs only characters of the line and of its quotients, and the lattice structure theory is reserved for the later Poisson-summation and structure pages.

scope_declines.name: §4.23, Theorem 4.26: translation between regular blocks with W_λ = W_μ is an equivalence
scope_declines.reason: The pair does not claim the block equivalence; it only uses the standard-module and simplicity behaviour across a single wall, which is proved from the Verma-flag computation.

scope_declines.name: C.3, Theorem C.6: a subgroup of the dual separating points is dense
scope_declines.reason: Density of separating subgroups is used together with inversion and biduality on the planned duality pair and is not needed for the closure, local-compactness or example claims of FR-15.

scope_declines.name: §1, the implication (c)⇒(a) in Theorem-Definition 1.1 (devissage producing a standard filtration)
scope_declines.reason: The pair never needs to construct a standard filtration from Ext vanishing; it only needs the multiplicity formula and Ext^1 vanishing for objects already known to be standardly filtered, so this converse is not consumed.

scope_declines.name: Bochner's theorem on finite groups and the transition to LCA Fourier–Stieltjes transforms, pp. 8–14
scope_declines.reason: The fetched edition of the notes cited as 'Taob note 9' contains no restriction or Strichartz material; the Strichartz interface is sourced instead to Williams §11.4. No FR-14 item depends on this source.

scope_declines.name: Section 7.1, Corollary 7.3: the inclusion of the dual into the compact group of all homomorphisms is an embedding iff the group is discrete
scope_declines.reason: This criterion compares the dual with all possibly discontinuous homomorphisms; no scaffolded FR-15 item or later consumer uses it, and it contributes nothing to local compactness or to the four examples.

scope_declines.name: §1, Lemma 1.5: generalized Verma modules M_{λ,n} admit standard filtrations
scope_declines.reason: This serves Lin Chen's alternative proof that projectives are standardly filtered; the pair proves that theorem through finite-dimensional tensoring of maximal-label Vermas, so this engine has no consumer.

scope_declines.name: §4.23, Lemma 4.25: a vanishing criterion for T_{χ1,V,χ2}
scope_declines.reason: The pair only needs the standard-module behaviour on a single wall and the adjunction; the general vanishing criterion for arbitrary translation functors is not used.

scope_declines.name: §16.3, Corollary 16.6(ii): every projective object is a free U(n−)-module
scope_declines.reason: Not needed by any claim of this pair. The free-U(n−) structure serves Etingof's Lemma 20.1 route to Ext vanishing, while the pair proves the Δ–∇ orthogonality by Lin Chen's pullback argument and never uses freeness over U(n−).

scope_declines.name: §24.2, two-sided ideals in U_θ and submodules of Verma modules
scope_declines.reason: This section studies the classification of projective functors and the KL problem; nothing in the pair's inventory or examples consumes its results.

scope_declines.name: Sections 7.4-8, natural transformation, duality theorem 7.36, structure and exactness
scope_declines.reason: Biduality, exactness and the natural transformation are exactly the subject of that planned pair; the present foundation stops before inversion and biduality by design.

scope_declines.name: Section 7.3, Theorem 7.14 second part: the dual of a product of compact groups is the direct sum of the duals
scope_declines.reason: Compact-product duality is not needed for the four concrete examples and is subsumed by the later biduality and exactness development of the planned duality pair.

scope_declines.name: §4.23, Proposition 4.28: Ξ_λ ≅ P_{w0·λ}
scope_declines.reason: The most singular block and the identification of the translated projective are not used by any claim or example in this pair.
